The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=3{y}^{2}-6(x+1)y+3{x}^{2}+6x+4,
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=3,\,b(x)=-6(x+1),\,c(x)=3{x}^{2}+6x+4.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=x+1.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=1$, we have

$$
y=z+x+1\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+1.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+1=3(z+x+1)^{2}-6(x+1)(z+x+1)+3{x}^{2}+6x+4.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+1 & =3((x+1)^{2}+2(x+1)z+{z}^{2})-6(x+1)(z+x+1)+3{x}^{2}+6x+4 \\ {z}^{′}+1 & =3{z}^{2}+1 \\ {z}^{′} & =3{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3 \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 3\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int 3\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =3x+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{3x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-(x+1)$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{3x+C} \\ y-(x+1) & =-\frac{1}{3x+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3x+C}+x+1 \\  & =x+1-\frac{1}{3x+C}\end{aligned}
$$
